title: Module 1 intro — System and Server Bring-up

lines: Welcome to Module One: System and Server Bring-up.
It's how a pallet of GPU servers becomes a working AI factory.

say.1: It's how a pallet of G P U servers becomes a working A I factory.

lines: Picture a team receiving thirty-two DGX nodes on a loading dock.
The deadline is Friday, so they rack everything and power it all on at once.

say.0: Picture a team receiving thirty-two D G X nodes on a loading dock.

lines: First problem: the nodes arrived on mixed firmware versions.
Half the GPUs throw errors that nobody can reproduce.

say.1: Half the G P Us throw errors that nobody can reproduce.

lines: Second problem: one swapped cable in the compute fabric.
A training job crawls, and it takes days to find the wrong port.
Third problem: one BMC still has its default password.
Anyone on the management network could power-cycle that node.

say.0: Third problem: one B M C still has its default password.

lines: So the team starts again with a disciplined sequence.
Plan, rack, power, cable, update firmware, secure, then validate, for every node, in order.
Lesson one walks through that bring-up sequence step by step.
You'll learn why order matters: firmware before validation, and security before production.
It also maps the networks of an AI factory.
Compute, storage, in-band, and out-of-band management each get their own fabric.

say.0: It also maps the networks of an A I factory.

lines: Lesson two covers the BMC, a small computer that manages the server even when it's off.
You'll lock down out-of-band access and see what the TPM adds to a trusted boot.

say.0: Lesson two covers the B M C, a small computer that manages the server even when it's off.
say.1: You'll lock down out-of-band access and see what the T P M adds to a trusted boot.

lines: Lesson three brings every HGX system to one firmware baseline.
You'll also learn to spot faults in logs and health tools.

say.0: Lesson three brings every H G X system to one firmware baseline.

lines: Lesson four plans power and cooling before a single server is installed.
One DGX can draw over ten kilowatts, so racks, circuits, and airflow all matter.

say.1: One D G X can draw over ten kilowatts, so racks, circuits, and airflow all matter.

lines: Lesson five is cables and transceivers.
You'll tell copper from optical, and match OSFP and QSFP modules to the right distance.

say.1: You'll tell copper from optical, and match O S F P and Q S F P modules to the right distance.

lines: Lesson six validates the hardware before anyone trains on it.
It checks GPUs, NVLink, and the network, then configures third-party storage.

say.1: It checks G P Us, en-vee-link, and the network, then configures third-party storage.

lines: Back on the loading dock, all thirty-two nodes pass validation on the first try.
Every node shares one firmware baseline, every cable is mapped, and every BMC is locked.

say.1: Every node shares one firmware baseline, every cable is mapped, and every B M C is locked.

lines: That discipline is exactly what the exam rewards.
Questions describe a real bring-up and ask what went wrong, or which step comes next.
This domain is thirty-one percent of the exam, one of the two biggest.
Lesson one starts with the bring-up sequence.
